svg.title: STAGE writing workflow — fifteen skills in order, one that reads across them, and what each one writes
svg.text: Sixteen skills · fifteen in order and one that reads across them · what each one writes · how the loops close
A new or existing paper repo wired into STAGE
Results snapshotted read-only, fingerprint per file
A story that holds; contributions become claims
The skeleton: page budgets, claims per section
Reading notes and a bib from fetched records
Where the paper stands, and the one next action
Every \cite key and claim checked against a note
Tables built from evidence, never typed
Every figure: a purpose, a source, a rendered PDF
Prose polished — never meaning, never a number
Every number traced to a fingerprint, or flagged
Every reviewer point answered; promises tracked
Build and lint gate, package, record, freeze
One takeaway, verified claims, figures reused
THE CYCLE REPEATS · THE LEDGER DOES NOT RESET
Rejected → a new cycls/<venue>_<year>/ against the same claim ledger, where the weakened
and unsourced claims are the first things the next attempt fixes. Accepted → the poster.
reads the outline and the ledger — and every other artifact
mismatch → repair the prose or the table
rejected → a new cycle against the same ledger
fails at poster size → the figure
Numbers live upstream. To fix one, fix it in STAR
and re-import — mates/ is never edited in place.
THE CLAIM LEDGER IS THE HUB
Every claim’s statements, evidence and status sit
Every number in manus/ traces to a fingerprinted
mates/ entry, or is written as \todo{…}.
/stage-… in Claude Code, Cursor, Pi, Qwen Code
$stage-… in Codex · /skill:stage-… in DSH, Kimi Code
reads every stage · run it any time
runs only when you name it
the ring through flow-status is the drafting loop, once per unit
9 and 10 re-run after any change to numbers or citations
